record.original_question: For sampled short-time Fourier transform phase retrieval of compactly supported or otherwise structured functions, which window functions other than the already analyzed Gaussian or specially constructed simple windows allow recovery up to a global phase from magnitude samples taken on a lattice?

evidence.quote: Question 8.6. What happens when w is not, e.g., the Gaussian or a simple window of the type utilized in [61, 94]? What other window functions w P L2(R) allow recovery up to a global phase from STFT magnitude measurements sampled on a lattice Ω (cf. also [52])?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a window function $w \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$, define the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) of $f \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ by
$$
V_w f(x,\xi) = \int_{\mathbb{R}} f(t)\,\overline{w(t-x)}\,e^{-2\pi i \xi t}\,dt, \qquad (x,\xi) \in \mathbb{R}^2.
$$
Two functions $f, g \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ are said to be equal up to a global phase if there exists $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$ with $g = e^{i\alpha} f$. Given a lattice $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ (i.e., a discrete subgroup of full rank), say that the sampled STFT phase retrieval problem with window $w$ on $\Omega$ is solvable on a class $\mathcal{C} \subseteq L^2(\mathbb{R})$ if every $f \in \mathcal{C}$ is uniquely determined, up to a global phase, by the magnitude samples $\{|V_w f(\lambda)| : \lambda \in \Omega\}$.

Characterize the windows $w \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$, other than Gaussians, for which there exists a lattice $\Omega$ and a natural class $\mathcal{C}$ (for instance, compactly supported functions, or other structured subclasses of $L^2(\mathbb{R})$) such that the sampled STFT phase retrieval problem with window $w$ on $\Omega$ is solvable on $\mathcal{C}$. In particular, identify general structural conditions on $w$ that guarantee or preclude recovery up to a global phase from lattice magnitude samples.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work establishes a "discretization barrier": for general $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ functions, uniqueness in sampled STFT phase retrieval on any lattice is unachievable regardless of the single window chosen. Workarounds use multi-window Gabor systems, non-lattice sampling sets (e.g., square-root lattices), or restricted function classes. The general question of which single windows admit lattice-based recovery on structured subclasses remains open, with only partial results for Gaussians and special constructed windows.

status_evidence.title: Non-uniqueness theory in sampled STFT phase retrieval
status_evidence.snippet: uniqueness via lattice-sampling is unachievable, irrespective of the choice of the window function or the lattice density
status_evidence.claim: Single-window lattice STFT phase retrieval is generally impossible on all of L^2.

status_evidence.title: Multi-window STFT phase retrieval: lattice uniqueness
status_evidence.snippet: conditions under which square-integrable functions can be uniquely recovered from spectrogram samples on a lattice using multiple windows
status_evidence.claim: Multi-window approaches partially circumvent the single-window lattice barrier.

status_evidence.title: Phaseless Sampling on Square-Root Lattices
status_evidence.snippet: Square-root lattices guarantee uniqueness of the STFT phase retrieval problem
status_evidence.claim: Alternative non-lattice sampling sets yield uniqueness results.
